chapter: Newark and first years in Harlem
title: Studying trumpet with Slossberg
summary: He studied intermittently with Slossberg, teacher of Bunny Berigan, a trumpet virtuoso who adored Armstrong but told him to be himself.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: I started to go to school again on the trumpet. I was going to school with a teacher name of Slessberg (PHONETIC). He was a great teacher. He's the one who taught Bunny) Berigan.
Slessberg. His book was (i method, i.e.). It's really a hard method.
How long did you study with him?
Well, I was studying off and on, you
know. (Inaudible). You study as long as you're in town.
So I met some friends and the man comes to town, his name is Billy Fowell, he was an orchestra leader. He was something like -- he was a conductor.
One moment. Now, when you were studying with Slossberg, did he ever give you -- now, what kind of musician was he, was he like a classical --
Oh, Slossberg, he was (Inaudible) he was a virtuoso on the trumpet. And I knew I needed this. I always knew I needed that.
But what did he play? Did you talk to him about what he thought of people like Louis Armstrong?
He adored Louis Armstrong. He adored him. He said the man's a star. Slossberg was a German man, I believe, or Russian.
No, Slossberg. All of them adored Louis Armstrong. See, he's a genius, you can't deny these things.
Well, did he ever talk in technical detail about what it was he liked about Armstrong's playing?

He -- no, no. He was too busy teaching me. Because he said, whatever he was doing, you are not him. You are an individual, too. Use what you have and you should be yourself. But you will. So I listened to that.
